recent_posts.title: daily.dev Hackathon
recent_posts.summary: daily.dev is hosting a 72-hour async hackathon open to all developers. Participants get full access to the daily.dev Public API and can build across three tracks: Developer Identity, Content Intelligence, and Content → Action. Any tech stack is allowed, AI tooling is encouraged, and the best submissions win 1 year of daily.dev Plus along with a feature on the platform. The only requirement is a public URL and a shareable output.

recent_posts.title: Help us escape the "Obsolete!!" delete button
recent_posts.summary: daily.dev is soliciting community feedback on what features or changes would make developers immediately install the browser extension. Suggested areas include better tab management, improved AI summaries, and deeper IDE integration, with an open invitation for other suggestions.

recent_posts.title: How to get hired through daily.dev
recent_posts.summary: daily.dev launched a career mode feature that connects developers with verified recruiters from tech companies. The platform uses developer activity to match candidates with relevant opportunities, and users can improve their chances by uploading their CV and setting job preferences in their account settings.

recent_posts.title: 10,000 developers have uploaded their CV to daily.dev
recent_posts.summary: daily.dev has launched a new developer-focused hiring platform where 10,000 developers have already uploaded their CVs. The platform aims to solve common recruiting problems by offering private matching, spam-free communication, and developer control over the process. Unlike traditional job boards, it integrates into the daily.dev platform where developers already engage with content, allowing career opportunities to find them organically without unsolicited contact or pressure.

recent_posts.title: Hug a user is here! Tell us what’s broken, we’ll fix it
recent_posts.summary: Daily.dev launches 'Hug a User' program where engineers dedicate up to half a day weekly to fix user-reported bugs and implement small features directly from community feedback. The initiative bypasses traditional development processes like tickets and sprints, focusing on quick fixes for annoying issues and small improvements that enhance user experience.

recent_posts.title: What makes you actually reply to a recruiter?
recent_posts.summary: A discussion prompt exploring what factors make software developers respond to recruiter messages on LinkedIn. The post asks readers to identify the key signals that distinguish compelling recruitment outreach from generic automated messages, focusing on elements like compensation, tech stack, company reputation, remote work policies, and career growth opportunities.

recent_posts.title: Help Us Decide: What’s Your Ideal Markdown Writing Experience?
recent_posts.summary: Daily.dev is seeking community feedback on two markdown writing interface options for their post creation feature. Option 1 offers live markdown rendering where formatting appears as you type, providing an all-in-one view without tab switching. Option 2 uses separate write and preview tabs, offering a cleaner writing space but requiring manual preview switching. The team wants user input to determine which approach better suits developers' writing preferences.

top_posts.title: New Reading Streaks System (beta)
top_posts.summary: Daily.dev has introduced a new Reading Streaks system to simplify the learning habit process. It tracks the user's current streak, longest streak, and total reading days. Unlike the previous Weekly Goal system, Reading Streaks allow users to continuously build on their accomplishments without the pressure of starting over each week. The system also includes a weekend freeze feature where the streak pauses over the weekend. Historical activities are retroactively counted towards the new streaks. Daily.dev plans to enhance the Reading Streaks system with features like leaderboards and badges based on user feedback.
